work_items.prompt: As a starting point, the Data and analysis officer counts the registered persons and households by neighbourhood (Óváros, Kertváros, Malomsor, Határrét) and compares them with the estimated population. Beside each neighbourhood they write the source and the date of the calculation, and name those that remain below the round's own minimum. The AI role may only count and summarise; material that goes before the public is approved by a person under rule RU-AI-1.
work_items.form_name: We show in which neighbourhoods the register is thin

work_items.title: We form an outreach team for each neighbourhood
work_items.description: For each thin neighbourhood, let us name a small team that looks for residents on the spot.
work_items.prompt: For each neighbourhood reported as thin, the Community liaison puts together a small outreach team of volunteers, association members and delegates of the district's council member, and names the team leader. The team works at the market, at the gates and in the associations, on paper and in conversation, asks for no device, and records nothing without the resident's knowledge. The AI role may only summarise and draft a proposed schedule; it does not decide the make-up of the team; material that goes before the public is approved by a person under rule RU-AI-1.
work_items.form_name: We form an outreach team for each neighbourhood

work_items.title: We word the call for the thin neighbourhoods
work_items.description: Let a draft of the call be prepared that explains why we ask residents to be in the register.
work_items.prompt: For each neighbourhood, the Communications officer writes a short, plain-language call that says what the council uses the data for, what can be corrected, and where the resident can turn. The call is also produced on paper for those who do not read notices. It may contain no promise that the office cannot keep. The AI role may only draft; material that goes before the public is approved by a person under rule RU-AI-1.
work_items.form_name: We word the call for the thin neighbourhoods

work_items.title: We find and remind those who have not yet answered
work_items.description: Let the outreach teams track who received the call and who has not yet responded.
work_items.prompt: The Community liaison keeps track of which household received a call and who did not come forward within the given time, then, with the teams, approaches them once more, politely. Whoever says no is not approached again. We record the result daily by neighbourhood. The AI role may only draft a reminder and count the approaches; material that goes before the public is approved by a person under rule RU-AI-1.
work_items.form_name: We find and remind those who have not yet answered

work_items.title: We recalculate the coverage and publish it
work_items.description: At the end of the round, let us measure the register's coverage by neighbourhood again, and publish it.
work_items.prompt: The Data and analysis officer recalculates the coverage by the same method as at the start and shows, by neighbourhood, how much it has risen. They publish the number together with the denominator and name the neighbourhoods that are still below the minimum, so that the next round is directed there. The AI role may only count and summarise; material that goes before the public is approved by a person under rule RU-AI-1.
work_items.form_name: We recalculate the coverage and publish it

work_items.title: Let us summarise what residents reported, by neighbourhood
work_items.description: Let us count how many people reported the same thing, and from which neighbourhood.
work_items.prompt: Take the reports that arrived between the rounds (for example the blocked drainage ditch in Malomsor or the repair of the benches in Óváros), merge those about the same thing, and count by neighbourhood how many people reported. Record the original case numbers so that the work can be traced back later. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only summarise and count, and a person approves the merge proposal; a person approves material that goes before the public.
work_items.form_name: Let us summarise what residents reported, by neighbourhood

work_items.title: Let us approve the handover and the budget in forints
work_items.description: Let a person decide whether we hand the case over, and up to what amount.
work_items.prompt: The Finance officer looks at the summary and decides whether the matter is the service company's task and up to what amount in forints it can be ordered (for example up to 150 000 Ft for repairing the lighting in Kertváros). We record the decision with name and date; nothing goes to the company without approval.
work_items.form_name: Let us approve the handover and the budget in forints

work_items.title: Let us word the handover and open the job with the contractor
work_items.description: Let a draft of the order to the service company be prepared.
work_items.prompt: Based on the approved limit, we word the order: where the fault is, in which neighbourhood, what the deadline is, and which reports it refers to. The opened job gets an identifier that links to the case numbers of the reports. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only draft a proposal, a person approves the sending of the order; a person approves material that goes before the public.
work_items.form_name: Let us word the handover and open the job with the contractor

work_items.title: Let us chase the service contractor when the deadline passes
work_items.description: If the company does not get back in time, let a reminder be prepared.
work_items.prompt: We watch the deadlines of the opened jobs, and if no feedback has arrived on a job, we draft a reminder to the company's contact person. We count how many jobs are running late and in which neighbourhood (Óváros, Kertváros, Malomsor or Határrét). The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only chase and count, a person approves the reminder before it goes; a person approves material that goes before the public.
work_items.form_name: Let us chase the service contractor when the deadline passes

work_items.title: Let us check on site that the work is done
work_items.description: Let a person check that the fault has really stopped.
work_items.prompt: The Community liaison checks on site whether the service company has done the work, and records whether the fault has gone away. If not, the job stays open, and we ask for a new deadline.
work_items.form_name: Let us check on site that the work is done

work_items.title: Let us notify those who reported, and close the job against the report
work_items.description: Let a draft of the notice about the closure be prepared.
work_items.prompt: After the on-site check, we draft a short notice to those who reported, and close the job against the case numbers of the original reports so that it is visible what became of them. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only draft a proposal, a person approves the notice before it goes out; a person approves material that goes before the public.
work_items.form_name: Let us notify those who reported, and close the job against the report

work_items.title: Let us gather in one place the reports that arrived between the two rounds
work_items.description: Let us take stock of what came in from Óváros, Kertváros, Malomsor and Határrét.
work_items.prompt: Collect into one list every report that arrived between the two rounds, through any channel: at the gate, at the market, by phone, by letter or on the ideas board. Beside each report keep its case number, the neighbourhood (Óváros, Kertváros, Malomsor or Határrét) and the channel. Do not throw anything out because it was badly worded. The AI role may only collect, group and summarise; under RU-AI-1 a person approves it before it is released.
work_items.form_name: Let us gather in one place the reports that arrived between the two rounds

work_items.title: Let us propose merging reports about the same thing
work_items.description: Let us find which reports are in fact about the same thing.
work_items.prompt: Go through the list and suggest a theme for each group of reports that concern the same problem, for example the pothole by the bridge in Malomsor. Merging keeps every reporter and deletes no report; a report criticising the council must not be left out or softened. The AI role may only draft a merge proposal and assign a report to a theme; under RU-AI-1 a person approves it before it is released.
work_items.form_name: Let us propose merging reports about the same thing

work_items.title: Let us count, once per person, how many reported a topic
work_items.description: Let us give, for each topic, the number of residents behind it.
work_items.prompt: For each theme, count how many different residents reported it, not how many messages arrived; someone who wrote five times about the same thing is one person. Add the breakdown by neighbourhood beside it. Also state how the count was done, so that anyone can check it. The AI role may only count and describe how the count was done; under RU-AI-1 a person approves it before it is released.
work_items.form_name: Let us count, once per person, how many reported a topic

work_items.title: Let us check that the number does not expose anyone
work_items.description: Let us make sure that a topic's number identifies no single reporter.
work_items.prompt: Before the numbers go out, compare them with consent and the retention rules. If fewer than three people belong to one theme in a neighbourhood, show no breakdown there, because it would reveal who reported. Public material may contain no name, address or contact detail. The AI role may only flag where a breakdown may be too narrow and draft corrective wording; under RU-AI-1 a person approves it before it is released.
work_items.form_name: Let us check that the number does not expose anyone

work_items.title: Let us publish the topic and the number of residents behind it
work_items.description: Let us make the approved topics public, with the number of reporters.
work_items.prompt: Publish for each theme the approved title, the number of reporters and the neighbourhoods, and what became of the matter: passed on, answered or still being looked into. We also use this list to put together the next round's questions. The AI role may only draft and summarise the text of the notice; under RU-AI-1 a person approves it before it is released.
work_items.form_name: Let us publish the topic and the number of residents behind it

work_items.title: Let us choose the single question and the answer options
work_items.description: One question, with closed answer options, that anyone understands unambiguously.
work_items.prompt: Ask a single question, one that the council is actually willing to act on according to the answer, and add a few closed answer options and a “don't know” option. Write down how long the vote lasts and what method we use to read the answers, before the first answer arrives. Do not ask a leading question, and do not ask two at once. The AI role (under rule RU-AI-1) may only draft versions of the question and the answer options; the question and the method description are approved by the Consultation lead as a person before anything goes before the public.
work_items.form_name: Let us choose the single question and the answer options

work_items.title: Let us get the question to every neighbourhood of Zöldhalom
work_items.description: The question reaches every neighbourhood, not only those who respond most often.
work_items.prompt: Send the question to every neighbourhood, including Óváros, Kertváros, Malomsor and Határrét, both through the contact details in the register and through the paper channel, with the same text. Record by channel how many people it reached. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only draft the text to be sent and the draft of the reminder; a named person approves the outgoing message before it goes.
work_items.form_name: Let us get the question to every neighbourhood of Zöldhalom

work_items.title: Let us find those who never answer online
work_items.description: Personal outreach in neighbourhoods from which hardly any responses come.
work_items.prompt: While the vote is open, look at which neighbourhood is sending few answers, and go there in person: to the market, the library, the neighbourhood meeting, where answers can also be given on paper. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only draft a reminder and compile the list of people to approach; a person approves the text for the approach and for sending the public reminder, and a person goes there.
work_items.form_name: Let us find those who never answer online

work_items.title: Let us count the answers once per person
work_items.description: One response per person, broken down by neighbourhood, together with the denominator.
work_items.prompt: Count each person's answer once, however many channels they sent it through, and record the answers as records by neighbourhood. Add the denominator beside it: how many voted out of how many the register holds in that neighbourhood. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only count and summarise; a person approves the numbers and the summary before publication, and a person also decides on any doubtful answer.
work_items.form_name: Let us count the answers once per person

work_items.title: Let us publish the short, dated result
work_items.description: One page, dated, with the denominator and what is needed to judge the result.
work_items.prompt: Publish the result on a single short page, with the date, the verbatim text of the question, the number of answers by neighbourhood and the denominator, and naming the neighbourhood from which hardly any answers came. Also write what the council will do with the result. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only draft the results page; before publication a person approves the text, and the publication is carried out by the Communications officer as a person.
work_items.form_name: Let us publish the short, dated result

work_items.title: Let us decide which neighbourhood we call together, and what we ask it
work_items.description: The neighbourhood's council member sets the place, time and questions of the residents' forum.
work_items.prompt: The district's council member decides whether the residents' forum is held in Óváros, Kertváros, Malomsor or Határrét, when and at what venue, and which two or three questions we ask residents for their views on. The venue must be accessible, and the time such that shift workers and families with children can also get there. Write down whom we want to reach, not just who usually comes. This step is a human decision; artificial intelligence does not fill it.
work_items.form_name: Let us decide which neighbourhood we call together, and what we ask it

work_items.title: Let us word the invitation, and send it out after approval
work_items.description: We prepare the text of the invitation; a person approves it before it is sent.
work_items.prompt: Under RU-AI-1, the AI role only drafts the invitation and the poster text with the neighbourhood's name, the time, the venue and the questions, and drafts a reminder for those who have said they will attend. It should use simple, short sentences and state how to send an opinion in writing in advance. The invitation and every reminder are approved by the Communications officer or the council member, a person, before anything goes out to the public.
work_items.form_name: Let us word the invitation, and send it out after approval

work_items.title: Let us find in person those who do not usually come
work_items.description: At the market, at the gate, in associations, we tell those who never respond online.
work_items.prompt: The community liaison takes the invitation to where people are: the Malomsor market, the Kertváros associations, the Óváros stairwells and the Határrét gates. Record who was approached and who could not be reached, by neighbourhood. Give a paper feedback sheet to anyone who cannot come. This step is done by a person; no AI role fills it.
work_items.form_name: Let us find in person those who do not usually come

work_items.title: Let us count those who attended, by person and by neighbourhood
work_items.description: From the attendance sheet we find out who came and which neighbourhood was left out.
work_items.prompt: Under RU-AI-1, the AI role only counts the attendance sheet: once per person, broken down by neighbourhood, and compares it with the number of people invited, so that we can see which neighbourhood was under-represented. It reports only a number, never a list of names. If the counter suggests an error, a person opens the original attendance sheet; a person approves the tally before publication.
work_items.form_name: Let us count those who attended, by person and by neighbourhood

work_items.title: Let us write the minutes and record what was said
work_items.description: The AI role prepares the draft of the minutes; the town clerk does the recording.
work_items.prompt: Under RU-AI-1, the AI role only summarises from the notes and the transcript of the audio recording what the speakers said, grouped by topic, with the requests and objections stated aloud listed separately. It must not attribute to anyone anything they did not say, and must not evaluate the contributions. The town clerk reads and corrects the minutes and a person approves them, and only then are they filed.
work_items.form_name: Let us write the minutes and record what was said

work_items.title: Let us publish what we heard and what will come of it
work_items.description: From the approved minutes we issue a plain-language summary to the neighbourhood.
work_items.prompt: Under RU-AI-1, the AI role only drafts the “you said, we listened” summary from the approved minutes: what came up, how many people were present per neighbourhood, and what the council commits to and what it does not, and why. A person approves publication, either the mayor or the council member as a named person, and only after approval does it appear in the neighbourhood and on the website.
work_items.form_name: Let us publish what we heard and what will come of it

work_items.title: Let us announce the drop-in session across the whole neighbourhood
work_items.description: Let us word the notice, and remind those who do not usually speak up.
work_items.prompt: Announce every office hour across the whole neighbourhood, not only on the streets from which the council member is usually approached: across the whole of Óváros, Kertváros, Malomsor or Határrét, on paper at the gates and at the market too. The announcement should state the time, the place, and that a report can be made without an appointment and without giving a reason. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only draft the announcement and draft the reminder for those who did not turn up on an earlier occasion; a named person approves the sending before anything goes public.
work_items.form_name: Let us announce the drop-in session across the whole neighbourhood

work_items.title: Let us receive residents in person
work_items.description: Let the council member sit down with the residents and listen to everyone for the same length of time.
work_items.prompt: The council member receives residents in person at the pre-announced place and time, in order of number, giving everyone the same amount of time. For anyone who cannot come, the community liaison can, at the council member's request, take down their matter on paper or in conversation. The role is elected; this step is never done by an AI (RU-AI-1).
work_items.form_name: Let us receive residents in person

work_items.title: Let us enter what we heard as reports
work_items.description: What residents brought orally should go into the register as a report on the form.
work_items.prompt: At the end of the office hour, on the same day, the council member records on the form as a report what they heard: who raised it (by neighbourhood, even without a name), what the matter is, and through which channel it arrived, so that what was said in person counts the same as what was submitted online. Write the report in the words the resident used, not in the council member's summary. The role is elected; this step is never done by an AI (RU-AI-1).
work_items.form_name: Let us enter what we heard as reports

work_items.title: Let us count the reports and sort them into topics
work_items.description: Let us show how many people reported the same thing, and from which neighbourhood nothing came.
work_items.prompt: Sort the reports received from the office hour into topics, count them once per person, and report by neighbourhood how many raised the same thing and which neighbourhoods raised nothing. We publish numbers, never persons. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only sort into topics, count and summarise; a person approves the summary and every publication, and opening an identifiable report remains a person's job.
work_items.form_name: Let us count the reports and sort them into topics

work_items.title: Let us write the feedback to the neighbourhood
work_items.description: Let us tell the neighbourhood what we heard and what follows from it.
work_items.prompt: From the numbers and the council member's decisions, draft feedback for the neighbourhood: what we heard, what the council member commits to, and what cannot be done, and why. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only draft the feedback and draft the acknowledgement to those who made a report; the council member approves the feedback before anything goes public.
work_items.form_name: Let us write the feedback to the neighbourhood

work_items.title: Let us count the reports past their deadline, by neighbourhood
work_items.description: From the register, let us pull out what has exceeded the committed deadline.
work_items.prompt: Before every council meeting, select the reports that have gone past their committed deadline and count them by neighbourhood: Óváros, Kertváros, Malomsor and Határrét. Next to each one, put the case number, the date of receipt and the number of days late, so that the list can be checked. Count the same matter once per person. Under rule RU-AI-1, the AI role may only count and summarise; a person approves public communication.
work_items.form_name: Let us count the reports past their deadline, by neighbourhood

work_items.title: Let us ask the owner about every late matter
work_items.description: Every late case should have a named owner who writes what the situation is.
work_items.prompt: Assign a named person responsible to every late case, for example Kovács Margit in Óváros or Szabó Béla in Malomsor, and send them a short reminder: what the reason for the delay is and when a resolution is expected. Write again after two working days to anyone who does not reply. Attach the replies to the same case. Under rule RU-AI-1, the AI role may only draft the reminder and chase; a person approves public communication.
work_items.form_name: Let us ask the owner about every late matter

work_items.title: Let us put together the list of late matters ahead of the meeting
work_items.description: A list by neighbourhood, with an owner and a new deadline for each case, for the meeting pack.
work_items.prompt: The list contains the late cases grouped by neighbourhood, with each one showing the name of the person responsible, the reason for the delay and the new committed deadline. At the top is the summary: how many cases are late, and how many of them belong to someone by name. A neighbourhood with no late case is also listed, with a zero, so that the gap does not look forgotten. Where there is no person responsible, write that, and do not fill it in by guesswork. Under rule RU-AI-1, the AI role may only summarise and prepare a draft; a person approves public communication.
work_items.form_name: Let us put together the list of late matters ahead of the meeting

work_items.title: Let us approve the list and present it at the meeting
work_items.description: The council chair personally approves the list and puts it on the agenda.
work_items.prompt: The council chair reviews the list, has corrected whatever is not right, and approves it in their own name before anything leaves the meeting papers. At the meeting the chair should also present orally the longest-late cases and ask those responsible what they need. Record the date of approval and the chair's name with the list. This step is done by a person.
work_items.form_name: Let us approve the list and present it at the meeting

work_items.title: Let us publish the accepted list, and follow up on the next one
work_items.description: After the meeting, the approved list should be published, and the commitments should appear on the next list.
work_items.prompt: After the meeting, publish the approved list on the office notice board and the website, readable by neighbourhood, with the names of those responsible and the new deadlines. On the new list for the next meeting, show separately what has been closed and what is still late, so that the progress is visible. Under rule RU-AI-1, the AI role may only prepare a draft and count; a person approves public communication.
work_items.form_name: Let us publish the accepted list, and follow up on the next one

work_items.title: Let us gather the matching record pairs
work_items.description: Let us compare the records of persons, households, businesses and properties, and mark the probable duplicates.
work_items.prompt: Go through the records of persons, households, businesses and properties in the register of Zöldhalom Town Council, neighbourhood by neighbourhood (Óváros, Kertváros, Malomsor, Határrét). Mark the pairs where the name, the address, the parcel number or the tax number match or are close to each other, and for each pair note which two sources it comes from. Do not merge anything yet, only collect the candidates. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only count and draft candidate pairs; a person approves the merge and public communication.
work_items.form_name: Let us gather the matching record pairs

work_items.title: Let us rank the candidates by safety
work_items.description: Let us separate the certain matches from the doubtful ones, because a wrong merge is harder to undo than a duplicate.
work_items.prompt: For each candidate pair, write down what proves the match: a shared identifier, the same parcel number or only a similar name. Form three groups: certain, probable and doubtful. Do not merge a doubtful pair, but leave it as separate records; it is easier to live with a duplicate than with a wrongly merged record. Count by neighbourhood how many pairs fall into each group. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only summarise, count and propose a classification; a person approves the merge and public communication.
work_items.form_name: Let us rank the candidates by safety

work_items.title: Let us check the data protection and records aspects
work_items.description: Before we merge anything, let us check what may be kept and what must be preserved from the two records.
work_items.prompt: The data protection and records officer reviews the certain and probable pairs: which record has valid consent, which must be kept for records reasons, and what cannot be carried into the merged record. The merge may not override a refused consent or a withdrawal. Record the result tied to the pairs. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only summarise and draft a reminder; a person approves the merge and public communication.
work_items.form_name: Let us check the data protection and records aspects

work_items.title: Let us ask the person concerned if the pair is not clear-cut
work_items.description: For probable pairs, we ask the person concerned to confirm with a short question, without an account.
work_items.prompt: For the pairs that are probable but not certain, reach the resident or business owner concerned at their given contact details and ask whether the two records refer to the same person, household, business or property. Note the answer on the record, together with the source of the answer. Do not merge the record of anyone who does not reply. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only follow up, draft a reminder and count the replies received; a person approves the merge and public communication.
work_items.form_name: Let us ask the person concerned if the pair is not clear-cut

work_items.title: Let us approve and carry out the merge
work_items.description: With the town clerk's approval, each person, household, business and property becomes a single record.
work_items.prompt: The town clerk goes through the certain and confirmed pairs in turn, and approves or rejects the merge pair by pair. The approved pairs become a single record that keeps both original sources and the date of the merge, so that it can be traced back. Mark the rejected pairs separately so that they do not come up again in the next round. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only summarise and draft the merge proposal; a person approves the merge and public communication.
work_items.form_name: Let us approve and carry out the merge

work_items.title: Let us count the result and publish it by neighbourhood
work_items.description: Let us show how many records became one and how many remain doubtful, in terms the public can understand.
work_items.prompt: Count by neighbourhood how many record pairs we merged, how many we rejected and how many remained doubtful, and how many records the register had before and after the merge. Compare the numbers with the denominator of the rounds, because we count once per person. Write the public summary in a short text that is easy to understand. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only count and draft a summary; a person approves the merge and public communication.
work_items.form_name: Let us count the result and publish it by neighbourhood

work_items.title: Let us put together the draft agenda
work_items.description: The town clerk compiles the agenda of the next meeting from the cases received.
work_items.prompt: Collect the matters received from the committees, the mayor and the council members (Óváros, Kertváros, Malomsor, Határrét), and put them in order as an agenda; for each item show who the proposer is and how much time they ask for. The AI role may only draft and order the agenda items and count the matters received; under rule RU-AI-1, a person approves before public communication.
work_items.form_name: Let us put together the draft agenda

work_items.title: Let us gather the proposals and summarise them
work_items.description: For every agenda item a short, readable summary is prepared for the council members.
work_items.prompt: For each agenda item, request the proposal, and if one is missing five working days before the meeting, remind the proposer. The summary should state what the material asks of the council, what it costs in forints, and which neighbourhoods it affects. The AI role may only write the summary, draft reminders about missing proposals, and count how many materials have arrived; under rule RU-AI-1, a person approves before public communication.
work_items.form_name: Let us gather the proposals and summarise them

work_items.title: Let us approve the agenda and publish the invitation
work_items.description: The mayor approves the agenda and the materials, and only then does the invitation go out.
work_items.prompt: The mayor reviews the draft agenda and the summaries, corrects or strikes out whatever does not hold up, and approves it in their own name. Only the approved agenda and its materials go on the notice board and the council's page; the time and person of the approval are recorded.
work_items.form_name: Let us approve the agenda and publish the invitation

work_items.title: Let us prepare the draft minutes
work_items.description: After the meeting the town clerk prepares the draft of the minutes from the recording and the notes.
work_items.prompt: The draft minutes should be prepared from the recording of the meeting and the notes: who was present, what was said item by item, and how each person voted. The town clerk and the mayor read and sign the draft, comparing it with the recording of the meeting. The AI role may only draft and summarise, and count those present and the votes; under rule RU-AI-1, a person approves before public communication.
work_items.form_name: Let us prepare the draft minutes

work_items.title: Let us record the resolutions, and keep them without silent rewriting
work_items.description: The approved minutes and the resolutions go into a register that is version-tracked and cannot be quietly altered afterwards.
work_items.prompt: Enter the approved minutes and every resolution in the version-control repository and the task manager with a resolution number, the vote ratio and the reasoning, where the council decided against the opinions it had heard. A later correction may be entered only as a new, reasoned version; the old version remains, and the correction is shown with the name of the person who approved it. The AI role may only draft the resolution register and count the resolutions and votes; under rule RU-AI-1, a person approves before public communication.
work_items.form_name: Let us record the resolutions, and keep them without silent rewriting

work_items.title: We sum up the incoming report for the moderator
work_items.description: The moderator gets a short, faithful summary, and we keep the original untouched.
work_items.prompt: From a report received by Zöldhalom Town Council between rounds, through any channel (for example, a report about the damaged paving of the Óváros market square), prepare a short summary: what the topic is, which neighbourhood it concerns (Óváros, Kertváros, Malomsor or Határrét), and whether someone else has already reported the same. Keep the original text word for word together with the name of the person who made the report, because moderation may not rewrite what was said. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only summarise, mark and count; a person approves merging a repeat and every forwarding; a person approves any material that goes public.
work_items.form_name: We sum up the incoming report for the moderator

work_items.title: The moderator decides: publish, hold back or reject
work_items.description: A person decides on every report, and we record the reason for the decision.
work_items.prompt: The community moderator publishes, holds back or rejects the report, and always writes down the reason alongside the decision. A report may be rejected only for abuse (for example insults, advertising or disclosing another person's data); criticism of the council, even if sharp, is a reason neither for rejection nor for holding back. We do not delete a repeat: we merge it and keep every person who reported. If in doubt, the report is published, and the doubt is recorded in the note.
work_items.form_name: The moderator decides: publish, hold back or reject

work_items.title: The data protection officer reviews what identifies anyone
work_items.description: Before publication it becomes clear which detail identifies a person, and a person decides this.
work_items.prompt: Before anything goes public, the data protection and records officer checks that the text contains no name, address, phone number or registration plate whose disclosure has no consent. Where there is one, we redact the passage and do not reject the report itself. The redaction and its reason are recorded, so that the person who made the report and the oversight committee can both see what changed.
work_items.form_name: The data protection officer reviews what identifies anyone

work_items.title: We word the reply to the reporter, with the reason
work_items.description: The reporter learns what happened to their report, and why.
work_items.prompt: The communications officer writes the reply to the person who made the report: whether we published, held back or rejected their report, on what grounds, and whom they can turn to if they disagree. The reply is sent back with the case number, through the channel of the report, and the reason is also made visible next to the published report. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only prepare a draft and remind; a person approves the reply and the publication; a person approves any material that goes public.
work_items.form_name: We word the reply to the reporter, with the reason

work_items.title: We count what became of the reports, by neighbourhood
work_items.description: Monthly it is visible how much was published, withheld and rejected, and where.
work_items.prompt: Each month the data and analysis officer counts how many reports we published, held back or rejected, by neighbourhood (Óváros, Kertváros, Malomsor, Határrét) and by reason, and names separately the neighbourhoods from which nothing arrived. We publish the share of rejections and holdbacks so that moderation stays publicly verifiable; if the share rises, it goes at the start of the account. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only count and summarise; a person approves the tally and its publication; a person approves any material that goes public.
work_items.form_name: We count what became of the reports, by neighbourhood

work_items.title: Let us draft a set of questions from the topics of the previous round
work_items.description: There should be a single draft, not three separate ones.
work_items.prompt: From the topics of the previous round and the most frequent subjects of the town's reports, the AI role drafts the first outline of the question set, marking by neighbourhood which question is meant for whom. It gives only an outline and publishes nothing. Under rule RU-AI-1, a person approves every outline before anything goes public.
work_items.form_name: Let us draft a set of questions from the topics of the previous round

work_items.title: Let us examine whether any single question misleads
work_items.description: The question should not suggest the answer.
work_items.prompt: The consultation lead reads the outline line by line: excluding every leading or ambiguous sentence, or one that asks two things at once, and also any that the council is unwilling to answer in substance. Whatever is rejected is returned with a reason. This step is done by a person.
work_items.form_name: Let us examine whether any single question misleads

work_items.title: Let us test it on paper with residents in all four neighbourhoods
work_items.description: It should be understood where no device is asked for.
work_items.prompt: The community liaison goes through the questions on paper with a few residents in each neighbourhood, in Óváros, Kertváros, Malomsor and Határrét, and notes down orally where they got stuck and what they understood differently. They do not ask for names and do not record personal data.
work_items.form_name: Let us test it on paper with residents in all four neighbourhoods

work_items.title: Let us count and sum up the trial round's remarks
work_items.description: Let us see which question most people get stuck on.
work_items.prompt: The AI role counts how many people got stuck, by question and by neighbourhood, and summarises the notes taken. It only counts and summarises; it does not carry through corrections. Under rule RU-AI-1, a person approves the summary before anything is changed or published on the basis of it.
work_items.form_name: Let us count and sum up the trial round's remarks

work_items.title: Let us word the paper sheet with the same questions
work_items.description: The sheet should ask literally the same thing as the online questionnaire.
work_items.prompt: From the approved question set, the AI role drafts the text of the paper sheet, with word for word the same questions in the same order, and flags the differences one by one. It prepares only a draft and sends nothing to print. Under rule RU-AI-1, a named person approves the sheet.
work_items.form_name: Let us word the paper sheet with the same questions

work_items.title: Let us check the data handling, and release the set of questions
work_items.description: Let us not ask for more than is needed.
work_items.prompt: The data protection and records officer checks that the question set and the sheet do not ask for unnecessary personal data, and that the two versions match. They send back any difference, and sign off a matching one for release. Signing is a person's job.
work_items.form_name: Let us check the data handling, and release the set of questions

work_items.title: Let us gather what residents reported, by neighbourhood
work_items.description: Let us count what residents reported about in the past quarter in Óváros, Kertváros, Malomsor and Határrét.
work_items.prompt: Take the items on the reports board from the past quarter and group them by topic and neighbourhood. Merging repeated reports should keep every person who reported, and we name separately the neighbourhood from which nothing arrived, because its silence is data too. Under RU-4, we do not open identifiable reports. The AI role may only summarise and count; under rule RU-AI-1, a person approves any material that goes public.
work_items.form_name: Let us gather what residents reported, by neighbourhood

work_items.title: Let us collect the council members' proposals from their own districts
work_items.description: Each council member writes down what they would ask in their district, and what they base it on.
work_items.prompt: Each council member proposes at most three questions about their district, writing next to each one from whom and when they heard it, because the voice of the district is not that of the loudest caller. The council member drafts and submits the proposal themselves; this step is done by a person and is not filled by an AI.
work_items.form_name: Let us collect the council members' proposals from their own districts

work_items.title: Let us compare the proposals with the residents' reports
work_items.description: Let us show which proposal has reports behind it, and which neighbourhood is left out.
work_items.prompt: Place the council members' proposals side by side with the numbers from the first step: how many reports support each proposal, which one rests on a single loud case, and which neighbourhood none of them touches. This gives a shortlist of three to five candidates, each with its supporting number. The AI role may only draft the comparison and count; it does not decide who makes the shortlist. Under rule RU-AI-1, a person approves any material that goes public.
work_items.form_name: Let us compare the proposals with the residents' reports

work_items.title: Let us word the shortlist's questions, and choose what the council will take on
work_items.description: The consultation lead decides which question the council is truly willing to act on.
work_items.prompt: Rewrite each candidate question as a clear sentence that asks about one thing, and write next to it what the council would do on the basis of the answer. The question that stays is the one the council is ready to act on; drop the one it is not, because an answer that is not acted on takes trust away. The political judgement belongs to the consultation lead. The AI role may only prepare wording variants; under rule RU-AI-1, a person approves any material that goes public.
work_items.form_name: Let us word the shortlist's questions, and choose what the council will take on

work_items.title: Let us choose the round's question, and put our name on it
work_items.description: The mayor or the council chair names the question that the council puts.
work_items.prompt: The mayor or the council chair designates the single question the round will ask, and writes down who and which neighbourhoods it was chosen for. If the decision goes against the weight of the reports, one person writes the reason, in their own name, into the round's report. This step is done by a person and is not filled by an AI.
work_items.form_name: Let us choose the round's question, and put our name on it

work_items.title: Let us publish what the council is asking, and why this
work_items.description: The publication tells residents what the council is asking and what led here.
work_items.prompt: Draft the message that announces the round's question, shows how many reports and which council member's proposal led to it, and says through which channels people can answer, including one that needs no device. Record the time of publication and the name of the person who approved it. The AI role may only prepare a draft and remind about sending; under rule RU-AI-1, a person approves any material that goes public.
work_items.form_name: Let us publish what the council is asking, and why this

work_items.title: We count what we heard on the subject of the decision
work_items.description: Let us tally the responses that came from the round by neighbourhood and by topic, according to the subject of the decision.
work_items.prompt: Pull up the records of the round that belongs to the decision, and count, by neighbourhood (Óváros, Kertváros, Malomsor, Határrét) and by topic, how many people said what, together with the denominator and the gaps in coverage. We report numbers, never persons. Do not rearrange the numbers to make the decision look better; where the circle of respondents was narrow, write that down. The AI role may only summarise and count; keeping to the rule (RU-AI-1), a person always approves any material that goes public.
work_items.form_name: We count what we heard on the subject of the decision

work_items.title: We put the decision and what we heard side by side
work_items.description: We record where the decision departs from what residents said, and on which points it agrees with it.
work_items.prompt: Take the decision that was made from the proposal and the minutes, and set the numbers from the previous step beside it. Mark point by point where the decision goes against what was heard, where it goes in the same direction, and where there is no answer to it. Name the divergence; do not smooth it over. The comparison stays part of the file recorded for the round, so that it can be traced back later. The AI role may only prepare a draft and compare; keeping to the rule (RU-AI-1), a person always approves any material that goes public.
work_items.form_name: We put the decision and what we heard side by side

work_items.title: The mayor states the reason by name
work_items.description: The reason against the decision is stated by the mayor or the council chair, in their own name.
work_items.prompt: The reason is written by the mayor or the council chair, who stands behind it with their name: why the council decided differently from what the majority of residents said, and what it weighed instead. This step can be done only by a person, because only a person can stand up for a decision. The reason should be short and easy to understand, refer to the comparison in the previous step, and not promise anything the council has not voted for.
work_items.form_name: The mayor states the reason by name

work_items.title: We publish: this is what we heard, this is what we did, and this is why
work_items.description: The published text says what we heard, what the decision was, and what the reason is.
work_items.prompt: Prepare a plain-language announcement for the Town Council's website and the neighbourhood notice boards of Zöldhalom: what we heard in numbers, what the council decided, what the reason is, and whose name stands behind it. Include also what changed because of what was heard; if nothing, write that too. It should also go up on paper beside the gate and the market stall, because not everyone reads online. The AI role may only prepare a draft and summarise; keeping to the rule (RU-AI-1), a person always approves any material that goes public.
work_items.form_name: We publish: this is what we heard, this is what we did, and this is why

work_items.title: We name the owner, and remind them of the deadline
work_items.description: The matter has a named owner and a deadline, and we publish this too.
work_items.prompt: Enter the person responsible by name and the deadline against the matter, and keep it in the town clerk's register so that feedback appears at the council's next meeting. If the deadline approaches and nothing is moving, remind the person responsible, but we do not make up for the omission ourselves. Make the name of the person responsible visible on the announcement as well. The AI role may only remind and prepare a draft; keeping to the rule (RU-AI-1), a person always approves any material that goes public.
work_items.form_name: We name the owner, and remind them of the deadline

work_items.title: We register the request and calculate the deadline
work_items.description: The town clerk gives a case number to the request for public-interest data and records the statutory deadline.
work_items.prompt: The Town clerk files the request received, for example Kovács Lilla's request about the renovation contracts of the Malomsor Market Square, gives it a case number, and records the date of receipt and the deadline for the reply (15 days from receipt). They confirm to the requester that we have received it. This step is done by a person; there is no AI role in it.
work_items.form_name: We register the request and calculate the deadline

work_items.title: We find and count the documents concerned
work_items.description: The data and analysis officer finds the requested documents in the register and counts them.
work_items.prompt: The Data and analysis officer finds in the register the documents named in the request, counts how many documents are involved (for example 7 contracts and 3 certificates of performance), and lists by department where they are. Where they cannot find one, they name it and do not leave it out. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only search, summarise and count; a person approves any material that goes public.
work_items.form_name: We find and count the documents concerned

work_items.title: We check what cannot be released
work_items.description: The data protection officer goes through the documents for personal data and trade secrets.
work_items.prompt: The Data protection and records officer goes through the documents and marks what cannot be released: the data of private individuals, trade secrets, documents preparing a decision. For every omission they write down the legal basis. This step is done by a person; no AI role decides what is left out.
work_items.form_name: We check what cannot be released

work_items.title: We write the reply or the reasoned refusal
work_items.description: The town clerk writes the reply with the documents that can be released, or the refusal with its legal basis.
work_items.prompt: The Town clerk writes the reply with the releasable documents, or, if something is not released, the refusal with its reasons and the possibility of appeal. A refusal always names the legal basis; it does not just say that it cannot be released. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only prepare a draft of the reply; a person approves any material that goes public.
work_items.form_name: We write the reply or the reasoned refusal

work_items.title: The mayor approves and signs
work_items.description: The mayor reads the reply and approves and signs it before the deadline.
work_items.prompt: The Mayor / council chair reads the reply or the refusal, and approves and signs it before the deadline expires. If a cost reimbursement is requested for copying the documents, they state the amount in forints (for example 1 200 Ft). Nothing goes out until then. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only draft a reminder about the deadline and follow up on where the signature is held up; a person approves any material that goes public.
work_items.form_name: The mayor approves and signs

work_items.title: We send the reply and publish what is of public interest
work_items.description: The communications officer sends the reply to the requester and publishes the public-interest data.
work_items.prompt: The Communications officer sends the approved reply or reasoned refusal to the requester within the deadline, and also publishes the public-interest data that was released, so that the same thing does not have to be requested again. They do not send the outgoing material until the mayor has approved it. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only draft the announcement and follow up on whether the reply has arrived; a person approves any material that goes public.
work_items.form_name: We send the reply and publish what is of public interest

work_items.title: We count what we asked and whom we heard from
work_items.description: From all the rounds of the year, we count how many questions we asked and how many out of how many responded, by neighbourhood.
work_items.prompt: Pull up the records of all the rounds of the year, and count, round by round and neighbourhood by neighbourhood (Óváros, Kertváros, Malomsor, Határrét), what we asked, how many answered out of how many, and where coverage remained incomplete. We report numbers, never persons; describe a narrow circle of respondents, do not dress it up. The AI role may only count and summarise; keeping to the rule (RU-AI-1), a person always approves any material that goes public.
work_items.form_name: We count what we asked and whom we heard from

work_items.title: We gather what changed because of what we heard
work_items.description: From the town clerk's register we pull out the decisions, the commitments and whether they were met.
work_items.prompt: From the town clerk's register, collect the year's decisions and commitments round by round: what we heard, what the council decided, who is responsible by name, and whether it was fulfilled on time. Where a decision went against what was heard, mark this; do not smooth it over. Remind the people responsible for commitments that have expired, but we do not make up for the omission ourselves. The AI role may only remind, count and summarise; keeping to the rule (RU-AI-1), a person always approves any material that goes public.
work_items.form_name: We gather what changed because of what we heard

work_items.title: We write the draft of the annual report
work_items.description: From the numbers and the changes, a plain-language draft report is prepared: this is what we asked, this is what we heard, this is what changed.
work_items.prompt: Write a plain-language draft report from the material of the previous two steps: what we asked, what we heard in numbers, what changed, and what did not; if nothing, write that too. With examples, broken down by neighbourhood, with amounts in forints where money is concerned (for example the Malomsor bench, 380 000 Ft). The draft cannot be published until a person has approved it in the next step. The AI role may only prepare a draft and summarise; keeping to the rule (RU-AI-1), a person always approves any material that goes public.
work_items.form_name: We write the draft of the annual report

work_items.title: The mayor reviews the report and approves it by name
work_items.description: The mayor or the council chair reviews the report and approves it in their own name before publication.
work_items.prompt: The mayor or the council chair compares the draft with the numbers and the register, corrects it if needed, and stands behind the report with their name. This step can be done only by a person, because a person is responsible for material that goes public; without approval the report does not go out. They must not commit to anything the council has not voted for.
work_items.form_name: The mayor reviews the report and approves it by name

work_items.title: We publish the report, and get it to residents
work_items.description: The approved report goes up on the website and on the neighbourhood notice boards, and also reaches residents on paper.
work_items.prompt: After the mayor's approval, publish the report on the Town Council's website and on the neighbourhood notice boards of Zöldhalom, on paper too beside the gate and the market stall, and send it to the groups of the rounds. A person hands in the scheduling of the announcement and the final form of the text. The AI role may only prepare a draft and remind; keeping to the rule (RU-AI-1), a person always approves any material that goes public.
work_items.form_name: We publish the report, and get it to residents

work_items.title: Let us check that the accounting module is ready
work_items.description: Let us check whether the accounting, task management and digital twin modules are switched off but can be switched on.
work_items.prompt: As finance officer, review at Zöldhalom Town Council the accounting, task manager and digital twin modules: whether each is switched off, and whether it can be switched on in a few minutes. Count how many open items there are on the 2026 budget line (for example 4 120 000 Ft for the Malomsor road repair). The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only draft, summarise, follow up or count; whatever goes public, a person approves beforehand.
work_items.form_name: Let us check that the accounting module is ready

work_items.title: Let us record the starting state in the digital twin
work_items.description: Let us save which services and assets exist today in each neighbourhood, so they can be compared once the modules are switched on.
work_items.prompt: As data and analysis officer, prepare a snapshot of the services and equipment of Óváros, Kertváros, Malomsor and Határrét. Put the starting numbers before the council, but do not add new data before switching on. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only draft, summarise, follow up or count; whatever goes public, a person approves beforehand.
work_items.form_name: Let us record the starting state in the digital twin

work_items.title: Let us check the approval limits and data protection
work_items.description: Let us make sure it is recorded who may approve what and up to what amount, and that the switched-off back-office part stores no personal data.
work_items.prompt: As data protection and records officer, compare the approval limits (for example above 500 000 Ft the mayor, below it the town clerk) with what is recorded in the system. Mark it if a limit is missing, and if the switched-off module would store any personal data. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only draft, summarise, follow up or count; whatever goes public, a person approves beforehand.
work_items.form_name: Let us check the approval limits and data protection

work_items.title: Let us put together the cost summary by neighbourhood
work_items.description: Let us prepare a cost summary by neighbourhood for the council, showing what switched-on accounting would provide.
work_items.prompt: As finance officer, prepare the summary of expenditure for the third quarter of 2026 by neighbourhood (18 760 000 Ft in total), referring to the source records. Send the draft to the town clerk; it can be published only after the town clerk's approval. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only draft, summarise, follow up or count; whatever goes public, a person approves beforehand.
work_items.form_name: Let us put together the cost summary by neighbourhood

work_items.title: Let us prepare the council proposal on switching on
work_items.description: Let us put on one sheet what changes, what it costs, and what happens if the council does not switch it on.
work_items.prompt: As town clerk, prepare a one-page proposal: what the second phase switches on, at what cost (estimated 1 250 000 Ft a year), and that the modules remain untouched even without being switched on. The proposal can go on the agenda only with the town clerk's signature. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only draft, summarise, follow up or count; whatever goes public, a person approves beforehand.
work_items.form_name: Let us prepare the council proposal on switching on

work_items.title: The council decides on switching on or leaving switched off
work_items.description: The council votes on whether to switch on the back-office modules, and we enter the decision in the report.
work_items.prompt: As mayor, put the proposal before the council, and enter the decision, the number of votes and the reasoning in the report. The modules can be switched on only after the council's decision; the reasoning for the decision must carry a person's name. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only draft, summarise, follow up or count; whatever goes public, a person approves beforehand.
work_items.form_name: The council decides on switching on or leaving switched off

work_items.title: Let us gather the fee rates in force
work_items.description: The finance officer collects the fees currently in force and the most recent amendments.
work_items.prompt: Collect the fees in force (for example the public space use fee of 2 500 Ft/day, the household waste collection fee of 1 800 Ft/month) and the council's most recent amending resolutions from Óváros, Kertváros, Malomsor and Határrét, with the date of entry into force next to each. The AI role may only draft the planned list of items, summarise the amendments, and count the items; under rule RU-AI-1, a person approves before public communication.
work_items.form_name: Let us gather the fee rates in force

work_items.title: Let us compare the items with the ordinance and the resolutions
work_items.description: The town clerk checks that every item matches the ordinance and the council's resolution.
work_items.prompt: The town clerk compares the draft item by item with the text of the ordinance and the council resolutions, lists the differences, and has the finance officer supply the missing references. The AI role may only draw attention to the missing references, summarise the differences, and count the items checked; under rule RU-AI-1, a person approves before public communication.
work_items.form_name: Let us compare the items with the ordinance and the resolutions

work_items.title: Let us approve the fee list in force
work_items.description: The mayor approves the list and the effective date, and only then can anything go out.
work_items.prompt: The mayor reviews the fee schedule and the date of entry into force, corrects or strikes out whatever does not hold up, and approves it in their own name. Only the approved version may go before the public; the time and person of the approval are recorded.
work_items.form_name: Let us approve the fee list in force

work_items.title: Let us publish the list on the notice board and on the site
work_items.description: The communications officer posts the approved version with its date and marks the previous one as superseded.
work_items.prompt: The communications officer puts the approved fee schedule on the notice board and the council's page with the date of entry into force, and marks the earlier version as obsolete. The AI role may only draft the text of the announcement and summarise the changes; under rule RU-AI-1, a person approves before public communication.
work_items.form_name: Let us publish the list on the notice board and on the site

work_items.title: Let us keep the earlier version, and note the publication
work_items.description: The records officer keeps the previous version and notes when the one in force went out.
work_items.prompt: The records officer keeps the previous schedule according to the retention rule, records the day of publication and the name of the approver, and counts how many versions are in force and how many archived. The AI role may only count the versions and warn if the day of publication is missing; under rule RU-AI-1, a person approves before public communication.
work_items.form_name: Let us keep the earlier version, and note the publication

work_items.title: Let us accept the application
work_items.description: The town clerk accepts the application, gives it a case number, and confirms it to the applicant.
work_items.prompt: Take in the request received (requester: Szabó Márta, Malomsor, Fő utca 12., attic conversion), give it a case number, and confirm receipt within the deadline under RU-7. The AI role may only draft the text of the confirmation and count the requests received; under rule RU-AI-1, a person approves before public communication.
work_items.form_name: Let us accept the application

work_items.title: Let us check the levy
work_items.description: The finance officer determines the amount payable according to the fee and levy list in force, and tracks the payment.
work_items.prompt: Determine the fee payable according to the published schedule (for example 18 500 Ft), and record when the payment arrived; under RU-11, we do not charge a fee before the schedule is published. The AI role may only count the unpaid fees and draft a reminder to the requester; under rule RU-AI-1, a person approves before public communication.
work_items.form_name: Let us check the levy

work_items.title: Let us record the inspector's finding
work_items.description: The building authority inspector examines the application and records the finding in writing.
work_items.prompt: Examine the request and the site, and record whether it complies with the requirements, what must be supplied, and on what condition the permit can be granted. The AI role may only summarise the outline of the finding and count the missing attachments, but the finding itself is written by the inspector; under rule RU-AI-1, a person approves before public communication.
work_items.form_name: Let us record the inspector's finding

work_items.title: Let us make the decision
work_items.description: The mayor, knowing the inspector's finding and the levy paid, grants or refuses the permit.
work_items.prompt: Decide on granting or refusing the permit on the basis of the inspector's finding, and give reasons for the decision; under RU-12, we do not issue a permit without approval. The AI role may only draft the outline of the reasoning for the decision, but may not make the decision; under rule RU-AI-1, a person approves before public communication.
work_items.form_name: Let us make the decision

work_items.title: Let us record the renewal date
work_items.description: The town clerk enters the permit's expiry date and renewal deadline in the client file, and notifies the applicant.
work_items.prompt: Enter the end of the permit's validity (for example 7 November 2031) and the deadline for the renewal application, and set a reminder for the applicant. The AI role may only draft the reminder and count the upcoming expiries; under rule RU-AI-1, a person approves before anything is made public.
work_items.form_name: Let us record the renewal date

work_items.title: Let us designate the period to be returned and the kind of report
work_items.description: The finance officer opens the upward report and selects the period (for example the third quarter of 2026) and the report requested by the national level.
work_items.prompt: Record which period and which national report it concerns, and which published ledger status and results it is built from (for example the quarterly expenditure total of 48 650 000 Ft). A person carries out this step; automation does not start it.
work_items.form_name: Let us designate the period to be returned and the kind of report

work_items.title: Let us put together the draft report from the published figures
work_items.description: The data and analysis officer collects from the published ledger and results the amounts falling on the report's lines.
work_items.prompt: Take the published ledger rows and results and assign them to the report's lines by department and neighbourhood (Óváros, Kertváros, Malomsor, Határrét); every line must show its source. The AI role may only word the lines, summarise and count them; under rule RU-AI-1, a person approves before anything is made public.
work_items.form_name: Let us put together the draft report from the published figures

work_items.title: Let us compare the report with the figures published locally
work_items.description: The data and analysis officer compares the draft line by line with what the town council published locally, and finds the differences.
work_items.prompt: Compare every amount in the draft with the published figure, count the rows that differ, and ask the row's owner for an explanation. The AI role may only compare, count and remind; under rule RU-AI-1, a person approves before anything is made public.
work_items.form_name: Let us compare the report with the figures published locally

work_items.title: Let us check that the report contains no personal data
work_items.description: The data protection and records officer reviews the report before it leaves the office.
work_items.prompt: Go through the report: only aggregate totals may appear in it, no names, addresses or individual items. The differences and the corrections stay in the register. A person carries out this step.
work_items.form_name: Let us check that the report contains no personal data

work_items.title: Let us approve the report and send it up
work_items.description: The town clerk signs the report and sends it to the national level; from then on the report is public.
work_items.prompt: In the town clerk's name, approve the report and send it to the national level, placing a copy of it next to the figures published locally. The AI role may not approve or send it; under rule RU-AI-1, a person approves before anything is made public.
work_items.form_name: Let us approve the report and send it up

work_items.title: We put together the draft call for applications
work_items.description: The finance officer records the budget, the deadline and the assessment criteria.
work_items.prompt: Record the amount of the civil support allocation (for example 4 800 000 Ft), the submission deadline and the assessment criteria, and put together the text of the call by neighbourhood (Óváros, Kertváros, Malomsor, Határrét) with equal chances for each. The AI role may only word the draft of the call; in keeping with the rule (RU-AI-1), whatever is put before the public is always approved by a person.
work_items.form_name: We put together the draft call for applications

work_items.title: We publish the call
work_items.description: The communications officer publishes the approved text and summarises it in plain language.
work_items.prompt: Publish the approved call on the office's page and on the notice boards, and make a short, plain-language summary of it. The AI role may only word and summarise the announcement; in keeping with the rule (RU-AI-1), whatever is put before the public is always approved by a person.
work_items.form_name: We publish the call

work_items.title: We receive the applications, and call for missing items to be supplied
work_items.description: The town clerk registers the applications received and has the missing items supplied.
work_items.prompt: Enter the applications received into the register (for example the 350 000 Ft request of the Malomsor Garden Friends Association), and if anything is missing, call on the applicant before the deadline. The AI role may only count the applications received and follow up on missing attachments; in keeping with the rule (RU-AI-1), whatever is put before the public is always approved by a person.
work_items.form_name: We receive the applications, and call for missing items to be supplied

work_items.title: We compile the applications for assessment
work_items.description: The data and analysis officer arranges the applications in a table according to the criteria.
work_items.prompt: Prepare an overview table of the applications: amount requested, neighbourhood, points per criterion; show the difference between the allocation and the amounts requested separately. The AI role may only summarise the applications and calculate; in keeping with the rule (RU-AI-1), whatever is put before the public is always approved by a person.
work_items.form_name: We compile the applications for assessment

work_items.title: The council decides on the grants
work_items.description: The mayor takes the proposal to the council, and a person carries the decision forward.
work_items.prompt: At the council's meeting, decide on the amounts awarded and record the decision with its reasoning; a person puts their name on the resolution. No artificial intelligence carries out this step. This step belongs to a person: an AI role never makes the decision or authorises the payment.
work_items.form_name: The council decides on the grants

work_items.title: We track the reports
work_items.description: The finance officer reminds applicants about their reports and checks the accounting for the funds.
work_items.prompt: Track whether the beneficiaries submitted their accounting by the deadline (for example for the use of the 350 000 Ft), and remind them if it is late; a person signs the acceptance of the accounting. The AI role may only remind, count and summarise the reports; in keeping with the rule (RU-AI-1), whatever is put before the public is always approved by a person.
work_items.form_name: We track the reports

work_items.title: Let us word the draft notice
work_items.description: The communications officer writes the draft notice from the triggering event and the official source.
work_items.prompt: Briefly write down what happened or what is expected (for example, because of the Malomsor water main break, the water service will be interrupted tomorrow between 8 and 14 hours), what to do, whom to call, and until when it is valid. In an emergency, naming the official source is mandatory. The AI role may only draft the text and prepare a simpler-language version; under rule RU-AI-1, a person approves before anything is made public.
work_items.form_name: Let us word the draft notice

work_items.title: Let us select the affected neighbourhoods and the channels
work_items.description: The data and analysis officer shows from the register how many households are affected, and assigns channels to every neighbourhood.
work_items.prompt: Name the neighbourhoods affected (Óváros, Kertváros, Malomsor, Határrét), and count the registered households per neighbourhood, for example 412 in Malomsor. Every announcement must include at least one channel that needs no device (notice board, loudspeaker, hand delivery), under rule RU-6. The AI role may only count the households affected and suggest channels; under rule RU-AI-1, a person approves before anything is made public.
work_items.form_name: Let us select the affected neighbourhoods and the channels

work_items.title: Let us approve the notice before it goes out
work_items.description: The mayor reviews the draft, the neighbourhoods and the channels, and approves it in their own name.
work_items.prompt: The mayor corrects or strikes out whatever does not hold up, and approves the final text, the neighbourhoods and the channels in their own name. Nothing goes out to the residents without approval; the time and person of the approval are recorded. Only a person can carry out this step.
work_items.form_name: Let us approve the notice before it goes out

work_items.title: Let us send out the approved notice on the designated channels
work_items.description: The communications officer sends the approved text to the designated neighbourhoods and posts it on the notice board.
work_items.prompt: Only the approved text goes out, word for word, to the recipients in the designated neighbourhoods, over the approved channels (SMS, email, notice board, loudspeaker). Record the time of the launch and the number of messages sent per channel. A person starts the sending, and in this step there is no automatic sending.
work_items.form_name: Let us send out the approved notice on the designated channels

work_items.title: Let us track the acknowledgements, and follow up on those missing
work_items.description: The community liaison counts who has acknowledged it, and personally follows up with those who have not.
work_items.prompt: Count, per neighbourhood, how many of those sent to have acknowledged the announcement, and for the households that have not acknowledged, ask by another channel or in person. At the close, publish the ratio of acknowledged to sent per neighbourhood, and name the neighbourhoods where it stayed under 80 percent. The AI role may only count the acknowledgements, summarise the ratios and draft a reminder for those who have not acknowledged; under rule RU-AI-1, a person approves before anything is made public.
work_items.form_name: Let us track the acknowledgements, and follow up on those missing

work_items.title: Let us take the booking request
work_items.description: The community liaison records the request received for the hall, room or event date.
work_items.prompt: Take the request on the form: who is asking (for example the Malomsor Garden Friends' Circle), which room (the main hall of Zöldhalom Town Hall, the small hall of the Óváros Community House, the Kertváros sports hall), on which day and from what hour to what hour, for how many people and for what purpose. The AI role may only word a summary of the request received and count the pending requests; under rule RU-AI-1, a person approves before anything is made public.
work_items.form_name: Let us take the booking request

work_items.title: Let us check for clashes, and suggest a time
work_items.description: The data and analysis officer checks whether the room is free, and if not, suggests a free time.
work_items.prompt: Check the request against the bookings already recorded and the calendar of council meetings; if the time is taken, suggest two free times in the same room. The AI role may only count the conflicting bookings and word a suggestion for the applicant; under rule RU-AI-1, a person approves before anything is made public.
work_items.form_name: Let us check for clashes, and suggest a time

work_items.title: Let us determine the fee according to the fee list
work_items.description: The finance officer calculates the rental fee in forints from the published fee list.
work_items.prompt: Calculate the fee according to the published fee schedule: the main hall is 6 500 forints per hour, the small hall 3 200 forints per hour, the sports hall 8 000 forints per hour, and local public-benefit associations get a 50 percent discount. A person decides on the discount and on any waiver of the fee. The AI role may only word the draft of the fee and count the hours booked; under rule RU-AI-1, a person approves before anything is made public.
work_items.form_name: Let us determine the fee according to the fee list

work_items.title: Let us approve the booking
work_items.description: The town clerk approves the booking and the fee, and only then does the booking become final.
work_items.prompt: The town clerk reviews the request, the conflict check and the fee, corrects or rejects whatever does not hold up, and approves in their own name. Only the approved booking goes into the room calendar and the accounts; the time and person of the approval are recorded. Artificial intelligence does not carry out this step.
work_items.form_name: Let us approve the booking

work_items.title: Let us send out the confirmation
work_items.description: The communications officer sends the applicant a confirmation of the approved booking.
work_items.prompt: Send the applicant a confirmation of the approved booking: room, day, duration, fee payable in forints, the payment deadline and the cancellation rule. The AI role may only word the text of the confirmation, write a reminder for unpaid fees and count the confirmations sent; under rule RU-AI-1, a person approves before anything is made public.
work_items.form_name: Let us send out the confirmation

work_items.title: Let us charge the fee, and open a receivable per payer
