work_items.description: The finance officer charges the fee according to the published fee list, and opens a separate receivable for every payer.
work_items.prompt: Record the charge: which fee (for example the quarterly waste collection fee of 4 800 forints per dwelling, the Malomsor market stall fee of 2 500 forints per occasion), who the payers are (for example Kovácsné Hegedűs Anna, the Malomsor Garden Friends' Circle), the date of the charge and the payment deadline. A separate receivable arises for each payer; the age of the arrears counts from the date of the charge. The AI role may only draft the charge and count the open receivables; under rule RU-AI-1, a person approves before anything is made public.
work_items.form_name: Let us charge the fee, and open a receivable per payer

work_items.title: Let us approve the charge
work_items.description: The town clerk approves the charged fees, and only then can anything go out to the payers.
work_items.prompt: The town clerk reviews the list of fees charged, the number of payers and the total amount in forints, corrects or sends back whatever does not match the fee schedule, and approves in their own name. The time and person of the approval are recorded. Artificial intelligence does not carry out this step.
work_items.form_name: Let us approve the charge

work_items.title: Let us send out the payment notice
work_items.description: The communications officer sends every payer a notice of the approved charge.
work_items.prompt: The notice contains the name of the fee, the amount in forints, the date of the charge, the payment deadline and the way to pay (for example the customer desk of the Óváros Community House, or bank transfer). The AI role may only word the text of the notice and count the notices sent; under rule RU-AI-1, a person approves before anything is made public.
work_items.form_name: Let us send out the payment notice

work_items.title: Let us record the payments, and compare them with the receivables
work_items.description: The data and analysis officer records the incoming payments and assigns each one to the right receivable.
work_items.prompt: Every payment is matched to the payer's receivable; a part payment reduces the receivable but does not close it, and an overpayment is marked separately. Give the list of discrepancies to the finance officer. The AI role may only word a summary of the discrepancies and count the settled and open receivables; under rule RU-AI-1, a person approves before anything is made public.
work_items.form_name: Let us record the payments, and compare them with the receivables

work_items.title: Let us prepare the aged list, and track the arrears
work_items.description: The finance officer prepares an aged list of overdue debts and proposes a reminder.
work_items.prompt: The list sorts the open receivables by age counted from the date of the charge: within 30 days, 31–60 days, 61–90 days, over 90 days, each with the number of payers and the arrears in forints (for example 17 payers, 81 600 forints in the 31–60 day band). A person decides on inability to pay or on hardship relief. The AI role may only draft the reminder and count the overdue receivables and the amounts; under rule RU-AI-1, a person approves before anything is made public.
work_items.form_name: Let us prepare the aged list, and track the arrears

work_items.title: Let us approve the reminders
work_items.description: The town clerk approves which arrears cases may be sent a reminder, and which receivable is left for an equity review.
work_items.prompt: The town clerk reads through the draft reminders and the list by age, takes out those with hardship relief or an appeal in progress, and approves the sending in their own name. Only the approved reminder leaves the office; the decision is recorded. Artificial intelligence does not carry out this step.
work_items.form_name: Let us approve the reminders

work_items.title: Let us gather the budget milestones by neighbourhood
work_items.description: The finance officer compiles the investment budgets and milestones for each neighbourhood.
work_items.prompt: Go through the milestones of the approved budget by neighbourhood: the renovation of the Óváros Community House 18 400 000 forints, the Malomsor pavement construction 9 750 000 forints, the roof repair of the Kertváros sports hall 12 300 000 forints. For each milestone write down the deadline and the allocated amount. The AI role may only count the milestones and word a summary of the allocated amounts; under rule RU-AI-1, a person approves before anything is made public.
work_items.form_name: Let us gather the budget milestones by neighbourhood

work_items.title: Let us group the expenditure by neighbourhood
work_items.description: The data and analysis officer assigns the payments to the budget milestones and the neighbourhoods.
work_items.prompt: Assign the completed payments to the allocations by milestone and by neighbourhood: for example, for the Óváros Community House 11 040 000 forints has gone out so far, 60 percent of the allocation. Mark a payment that has no milestone. The AI role may only count the unclassified payments and word a comparative summary; under rule RU-AI-1, a person approves before anything is made public.
work_items.form_name: Let us group the expenditure by neighbourhood

work_items.title: Let us check the completion certificates and the retention
work_items.description: The finance officer compares the completion certificates with the payments, and checks the retained amount.
work_items.prompt: For every payment, find the signed completion certificate and check the retention: under the contract, 5 percent of the invoice value is held back until the end of the warranty period (for example 180 000 forints on an invoice of 3 600 000 forints). If there is no certificate, mark the payment and let a person decide on it. The AI role may only write a reminder about the missing certificates and count the retained items; under rule RU-AI-1, a person approves before anything is made public.
work_items.form_name: Let us check the completion certificates and the retention

work_items.title: Let us approve the statement by neighbourhood
work_items.description: The town clerk approves the statement, and only then can anything be made public.
work_items.prompt: The town clerk reviews the statement by neighbourhood, the milestones, the certificates and the retention, corrects or returns whatever does not hold up, and approves in their own name. Only the approved statement may be published; the time and person of the approval are recorded. Artificial intelligence does not carry out this step.
work_items.form_name: Let us approve the statement by neighbourhood

work_items.title: Let us publish the budget and expenditure statement
work_items.description: The communications officer publishes the approved statement on the notice board and on the site.
work_items.prompt: Put the approved statement on the notice board of Zöldhalom Town Hall and on the page, by neighbourhood: allocation, amount paid, retention in forints and the state of the milestone, in plain language, with its date. The AI role may only word the text of the announcement and count the neighbourhoods published; under rule RU-AI-1, a person approves before anything is made public.
work_items.form_name: Let us publish the budget and expenditure statement

work_items.title: Let us gather the residents' questions about the statement
work_items.description: The community liaison collects the residents' questions and passes them on to the finance officer.
work_items.prompt: Collect what residents ask about the published figures (for example the Malomsor Garden Friends' Circle about the cost of the pavement construction), and hand it to the finance officer to answer. We do not release the answers without the town clerk's approval. The AI role may only count the questions received and write a reminder about the unanswered ones; under rule RU-AI-1, a person approves before anything is made public.
work_items.form_name: Let us gather the residents' questions about the statement

work_items.title: We ask the question in the chat
work_items.description: The council risk reader writes their question in the chat.
work_items.prompt: The Council risk reader writes in the chat what they would like to know, for example: what are the hazards to the water supply of the Malomsor Market Square, or what depends on the backup pump. It is one of the five simple questions or a request for the biggest gaps. A person carries out this step, no AI role is in it.
work_items.form_name: We ask the question in the chat

work_items.title: We look for the answer in the register
work_items.description: The assistant answers the five simple questions from the register.
work_items.prompt: The Risk chat assistant looks up in the register the hazards, consequences, preventive and mitigating measures that belong to the question, or what depends on a check, and answers from the register. What is not in it, it says so and does not make it up. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only summarise and follow up; whatever is put before the public is approved by a person.
work_items.form_name: We look for the answer in the register

work_items.title: We offer choice buttons if two names match
work_items.description: If the names of two risks or controls fit the question, the assistant offers buttons.
work_items.prompt: If a name in the question fits two risks or two checks, for example Backup pump and Backup pump station, the Risk chat assistant offers choice buttons and answers after the choice is made. It does not guess. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only word and follow up; whatever is put before the public is approved by a person.
work_items.form_name: We offer choice buttons if two names match

work_items.title: We list and count the biggest gaps
work_items.description: The assistant lists and counts the biggest gaps by owner.
work_items.prompt: The Risk chat assistant lists the biggest gaps by owner and counts how many gaps there are per department, for example 3 gaps in the Urban Operations Department. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only count and summarise; whatever is put before the public is approved by a person.
work_items.form_name: We list and count the biggest gaps

work_items.title: The department head checks the answer concerning their own service
work_items.description: The department head compares the answer with the risks of their own service.
work_items.prompt: The Department head (risk owner) compares the answer received with the risks of their own service, and signals if something is missing or out of date. They see only their own service. A person carries out this step, no AI role is in it.
work_items.form_name: The department head checks the answer concerning their own service

work_items.title: The mayor approves what goes into the council material
work_items.description: The mayor approves before the answer goes to the council or to the public.
work_items.prompt: The Mayor / council chair reads the answer and the list of gaps, and approves them before they go into the council papers or before the public. Until then nothing goes out. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only word a reminder about the answers awaiting approval and follow up on where they got stuck; whatever is put before the public is approved by a person.
work_items.form_name: The mayor approves what goes into the council material

work_items.title: We submit the conflict of interest declaration
work_items.description: The council member submits their declaration of interests.
work_items.prompt: The Council member submits their declaration of conflict of interest: they name their businesses, offices and the interests of their close relatives, for example their 12 percent ownership share in Malomsor Waterworks Ltd. A person carries out this step, no AI role is in it.
work_items.form_name: We submit the conflict of interest declaration

work_items.title: We register it, and compare it with the agenda
work_items.description: The data officer registers the declaration and notes which agenda item it affects.
work_items.prompt: The Data and analysis officer enters the declaration in the register and compares it with the agenda of the next meeting, indicating which agenda item it may affect, for example the renewal of the waterworks contract. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only summarise and follow up; it does not decide on the involvement, and whatever is put before the public is approved by a person.
work_items.form_name: We register it, and compare it with the agenda

work_items.title: The town clerk assesses the involvement, and records the approval limit
work_items.description: The town clerk decides whether the council member must recuse themselves, and writes on the role how large an amount it may approve.
work_items.prompt: The Town clerk judges whether the council member must recuse themselves from the agenda item concerned, and records for the approving role the largest amount it may approve in one act, for example 500 000 forints. The limit is written to the role, not kept in someone's head (RU-12); leaving it out means there is no upper limit, so giving it is mandatory. A person carries out this step, no AI role is in it.
work_items.form_name: The town clerk assesses the involvement, and records the approval limit

work_items.title: The finance officer checks the amount against the recorded limit
work_items.description: Before approval, the finance officer checks that the amount is within the limit of the approving role.
work_items.prompt: The Finance officer compares the amount awaiting approval, for example 720 000 forints, with the limit recorded that day for the approving role (RU-12). If the amount is above the limit, the system refuses the approval; that role cannot approve the request, and it goes to a role whose limit covers it. A person carries out this step, no AI role is in it.
work_items.form_name: The finance officer checks the amount against the recorded limit

work_items.title: We remind whoever's declaration is still missing
work_items.description: The assistant counts the missing declarations and drafts a reminder.
work_items.prompt: The Communications officer counts how many council members' declarations are still missing, for example 3 of the 15, and drafts a reminder for them. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only count, word and follow up; a person approves the reminder before it goes out.
work_items.form_name: We remind whoever's declaration is still missing

work_items.title: The mayor approves the register and the limits
work_items.description: The mayor approves the register of declarations and the limits written on the roles.
work_items.prompt: The Mayor / council chair approves the register of declarations and the limits recorded for the roles. Their own approval is also valid only up to the limit written to their own role (RU-12): what is above it they cannot approve, and another role must be found. A person carries out this step, no AI role is in it.
work_items.form_name: The mayor approves the register and the limits

work_items.title: We describe the new risk and name the owner
work_items.description: The department head names the risk, the worst case and the owner.
work_items.prompt: The Department head (risk owner) names the new risk in the phone app or in the chat, for example the winter freezing of the Zöldhalom Water Tower, describes the worst case, and names the owner, for example Kovács Dezső. A person carries out this step, no AI role is in it.
work_items.form_name: We describe the new risk and name the owner

work_items.title: We draft the causes, the consequences and the controls
work_items.description: The assistant gives a bow-tie diagram sketch from the description.
work_items.prompt: The Risk drafting assistant gives, from the description, a draft of the causes (for example prolonged frost, failure of the heating cable), the consequences (for example water shortage in 400 households) and the proposed preventive and mitigating measures. It does not save the draft. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only word; whatever would be saved is approved by a person.
work_items.form_name: We draft the causes, the consequences and the controls

work_items.title: We review and approve the draft
work_items.description: The department head corrects the sketch and approves it before anything is saved.
work_items.prompt: The Department head (risk owner) goes through the draft, corrects, supplements or deletes the wrong lines, and approves. Nothing goes into the register without approval. A person carries out this step.
work_items.form_name: We review and approve the draft

work_items.title: We check that the owner is known
work_items.description: The town clerk checks that the named owner appears in the roster.
work_items.prompt: The Town clerk checks that the owner named is a known person in the directory. If not, the entry is rejected, the risk is not saved, and the department head names another owner. A person carries out this step.
work_items.form_name: We check that the owner is known

work_items.title: We save the risk, and place the controls on the causes and the consequences
work_items.description: The department head saves the risk with its causes, consequences and controls.
work_items.prompt: The Department head (risk owner) saves the approved risk with its causes and consequences, and then places the controls on the cause or consequence they protect against, for example the backup heating cable on the frost. The risk goes into the register as a draft. A person carries out this step.
work_items.form_name: We save the risk, and place the controls on the causes and the consequences

work_items.title: The council reader sees the risk in the register
work_items.description: The council risk reader sees the new risk with its owner in the register.
work_items.prompt: The Council risk reader looks in the register at the new risk with its owner, its causes, its consequences and its controls. A person carries out this step.
work_items.form_name: The council reader sees the risk in the register

work_items.title: We attach a report to the control
work_items.description: The department head selects the control and attaches the report of the test or check to it.
work_items.prompt: The Department head (risk owner) selects the control in the phone app, for example the backup heating cable of the Zöldhalom Water Tower, which is now unproven, and attaches the winter test report to it. A person carries out this step, no AI role is in it.
work_items.form_name: We attach a report to the control

work_items.title: We summarise the report, and suggest a result
work_items.description: The assistant gives a short summary of the report and a suggested result (passed or failed).
work_items.prompt: The Risk chat assistant drafts from the attached report a short summary and a proposed result (passed or failed), for example: the heating cable held the temperature for three hours in the test. It does not record the result. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only word; whatever would be recorded is approved by a person.
work_items.form_name: We summarise the report, and suggest a result

work_items.title: We approve the assessment, and record the evidence
work_items.description: The department head approves or corrects the summary and the result, then records the evidence.
work_items.prompt: The Department head (risk owner) goes through the summary and the proposed result, corrects it if needed, then approves it and records the evidence against the control. Nothing goes into the register without approval. With a successful result the control goes from unproven to proven; with an unsuccessful one, to failed. A person carries out this step.
work_items.form_name: We approve the assessment, and record the evidence

work_items.title: We count the actions by status
work_items.description: The assistant counts the risk's controls: how many are proven, weak, unproven and failed.
work_items.prompt: The Risk chat assistant counts from the register the risk's controls by status: how many are proven, weak, unproven and failed, and shows which one changed. The AI role (RU-AI-1) only reads and counts; it changes nothing and does not make up a number. Whatever would be made public is first approved by a person.
work_items.form_name: We count the actions by status

work_items.title: The council reader sees the new status
work_items.description: The council risk reader sees the control's new status in the register.
work_items.prompt: The Council risk reader looks in the register at the new status of the control and the evidence attached to it. A person carries out this step.
work_items.form_name: The council reader sees the new status

work_items.title: We review the gaps caused by outdated evidence
work_items.description: The department head sees on the gap list the measures whose latest evidence is older than the configured number of days.
work_items.prompt: The Department head (risk owner) looks on the gaps list at the controls whose latest evidence is older than the set number of days, for example 30 days; these fall back to unproven. The going stale shows up only as a gap: no message is sent to anyone, and no task is created by itself. A person carries out this step.
work_items.form_name: We review the gaps caused by outdated evidence

work_items.title: We look at our own gaps
work_items.description: The department head opens the list of gaps, filtered to their own risks.
work_items.prompt: The Department head (risk owner) opens the list of gaps filtered to their own risks, and selects one, for example that the backup heating cable of the Zöldhalom Water Tower has not yet been assessed. A person carries out this step, no AI role is in it.
work_items.form_name: We look at our own gaps

work_items.title: We prepare a suggestion for the action and the deadline
work_items.description: The assistant suggests an action and a deadline for the gap.
work_items.prompt: The Risk chat assistant drafts from the selected gap a proposal for the action's title, the owner and the deadline, and counts how many open actions the owner already has. It does not save the proposal and does not create a task. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only word and count; a person approves the creation.
work_items.form_name: We prepare a suggestion for the action and the deadline

work_items.title: We approve and create the action
work_items.description: The department head approves the suggestion and creates the action with a link to the task.
work_items.prompt: The Department head (risk owner) goes through the proposal, corrects the title or the deadline, approves it, and creates the action. The action creates an ordinary task on the council's board, with an owner and a deadline, and links to it. Nothing is created without approval. A person carries out this step.
work_items.form_name: We approve and create the action

work_items.title: The owner carries out the task on the board
work_items.description: The owner carries out and closes the task on the council board.
work_items.prompt: The owner, for example Kovács Dezső, opens the task on the council board, carries out the check of the backup heating cable, and marks it done. A person carries out this step.
work_items.form_name: The owner carries out the task on the board

work_items.title: We close the action and assess the control
work_items.description: The department head marks the action as done and assesses the control.
work_items.prompt: The Department head (risk owner), based on the finished task, marks the action done, then gives the assessment of the control's design and coverage. After the assessment the gap comes off the list. A person carries out this step.
work_items.form_name: We close the action and assess the control

work_items.title: At the council meeting we see that the task has been closed
work_items.description: The town clerk sees on the overdue tasks list that the task is no longer on it.
work_items.prompt: At the council meeting, the Town clerk looks at the list of overdue tasks and sees that the closed task is no longer on it, and that the gap has come off the list of gaps. A person carries out this step.
work_items.form_name: At the council meeting we see that the task has been closed

work_items.title: We ask for the risk part for the meeting pack
work_items.description: On the day of the meeting, the town clerk asks for the risk part of the pack.
work_items.prompt: On the day of the meeting, the Town clerk opens the council meeting pack and asks for the risk section, for example for the meeting of 12 May. A person carries out this step, no AI role is in it.
work_items.form_name: We ask for the risk part for the meeting pack

work_items.title: We gather the risks and write a draft
work_items.description: The assistant lists the failed controls, the serious gaps and the overdue actions.
work_items.prompt: The Risk chat assistant lists from the register the failing controls, the serious gaps and the overdue actions with their owners, for example that the action for the backup heating cable of the Zöldhalom Water Tower has been overdue for 9 days, counts them, and drafts a text. It does not publish the draft and does not put it in the pack. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only collect, count and word; a person approves the publication.
work_items.form_name: We gather the risks and write a draft

work_items.title: The owners review their own lines
work_items.description: The department heads correct their own lines in the draft.
work_items.prompt: The Department head (risk owner) goes through their own lines in the draft, corrects the owner or the deadline if they differ from reality, and signals if an action has been completed in the meantime. A person carries out this step.
work_items.form_name: The owners review their own lines

work_items.title: We review the risk part for clarity
work_items.description: The council risk reader reviews whether the council understands it.
work_items.prompt: The Council risk reader reads through the risk section, and signals if a line is not understandable to the council members, or if the owner's name is missing from beside it. A person carries out this step.
work_items.form_name: We review the risk part for clarity

work_items.title: We approve it and attach it to the meeting material
work_items.description: The town clerk approves the risk part and attaches it to the meeting's agenda material.
work_items.prompt: The Town clerk goes through the risk section, approves it, and attaches it to the agenda papers of the meeting. Nothing goes into the pack without approval, and nothing becomes public. A person carries out this step.
work_items.form_name: We approve it and attach it to the meeting material

work_items.title: At the meeting we go through the risks
work_items.description: At the meeting, the mayor presents the failed controls and the overdue actions.
work_items.prompt: At the meeting, the Mayor / council chair goes through the risk section and asks the owners about the overdue actions. A person carries out this step.
work_items.form_name: At the meeting we go through the risks

work_items.title: We gather the addresses without a neighbourhood
work_items.description: We collect the records that have an address or a point but no neighbourhood.
work_items.prompt: The Data and analysis officer collects from the register the people, households and businesses that have an address or a map point but whose neighbourhood field is empty, for example Gyár utca 14. and Malom köz 3. They count them, and write beside them the source and the date of the collection. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only collect, count and draft; a person approves any figure that goes before the public, under rule RU-AI-1.
work_items.form_name: We gather the addresses without a neighbourhood

work_items.title: We find the neighbourhood from the point
work_items.description: For every collected record's point, we look up the neighbourhood whose boundary contains it.
work_items.prompt: For the point of every collected record, the Data and analysis officer looks up which neighbourhood (Óváros, Kertváros, Malomsor or Határrét) has a boundary containing it, taking the innermost boundary, and writes the calculated neighbourhood beside the record as a suggestion. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only collect, count and draft; a person approves any figure that goes before the public, under rule RU-AI-1.
work_items.form_name: We find the neighbourhood from the point

work_items.title: We flag the discrepancies and the points outside the boundary
work_items.description: We put on a separate list the records where the entered and the calculated neighbourhood differ, or the point is inside no boundary.
work_items.prompt: The Data and analysis officer puts on a separate list the records where the neighbourhood entered by hand differs from the one calculated from the point, and also those whose point is not inside any neighbourhood's boundary, for example at the end of the dirt track beside Határrét. They do not overwrite the entered neighbourhood, only flag the difference. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only collect, count and draft; a person approves any figure that goes before the public, under rule RU-AI-1.
work_items.form_name: We flag the discrepancies and the points outside the boundary

work_items.title: The officer decides on the discrepancies
work_items.description: The officer decides record by record which neighbourhood stays, or whether the record waits for a site check.
work_items.prompt: The Data and analysis officer goes through the flagged records, and for each decides whether the entered or the calculated neighbourhood stays, or whether the record outside the boundary waits for an on-site check; the decision and its reason are recorded on the record. A person carries out this step, no AI role is in it.
work_items.form_name: The officer decides on the discrepancies

work_items.title: We count the records by neighbourhood
work_items.description: After the decision, we count the records by neighbourhood, and a person approves the number.
work_items.prompt: After the decisions, the Data and analysis officer counts the records per neighbourhood, putting those still without a neighbourhood on a separate line, and drafts a text of the figures; the draft goes nowhere until a person has approved it. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only collect, count and draft; a person approves any figure that goes before the public, under rule RU-AI-1.
work_items.form_name: We count the records by neighbourhood

work_items.title: We receive the report without identity
work_items.description: The data protection and records officer receives the report without a name, account or contact details.
work_items.prompt: The Data protection and records officer receives the report through any channel, for example from the box placed at the Malomsor gate or from the phone customer line, and does not ask for a name, address or contact details. The reporter's account and the details of the sending are not kept with the case. A person carries out this step, no AI role is in it.
work_items.form_name: We receive the report without identity

work_items.title: The submitter gets a receipt code, not a name
work_items.description: The community liaison hands over the receipt code with which the submitter can later check the status of the case.
work_items.prompt: The Community liaison hands over a random receipt code, for example NY-4821, with which the sender can ask about the status of the case without giving a name. The code contains no personal data, and the register does not tie it to a name. A person carries out this step, no AI role is in it.
work_items.form_name: The submitter gets a receipt code, not a name

work_items.title: We judge the sensitivity of the report
work_items.description: The owner decides whether the report is sensitive and who may see it.
work_items.prompt: The Data protection and records officer reads the report and decides whether it is sensitive: for example, whether it is about the conduct of a public employee, the health of a neighbour or the cash handling of the Kertváros Community House. A sensitive report may be read only by the officer and the department head it is addressed to. A person carries out this step, no AI role is in it.
work_items.form_name: We judge the sensitivity of the report

work_items.title: A person removes the identifying details
work_items.description: The owner removes from the text anything from which the submitter or the person concerned could be worked out.
work_items.prompt: The Data protection and records officer goes through the text line by line, and removes the names, addresses, licence plates, exact times and the turns of phrase from which the sender could be guessed. The original text does not go further, only the cleaned version. A person carries out this step, no AI role is in it.
work_items.form_name: A person removes the identifying details

work_items.title: A suggestion for the appropriate department
work_items.description: The assistant writes a draft from the cleaned text and suggests which department the matter belongs to.
work_items.prompt: The Data and analysis officer writes a short summary from the cleaned text, and proposes which department the case belongs to, for example the Óváros road maintenance or the social services office. They do not receive the original text and do not look for the sender. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only draft, summarise and make a suggestion; the officer in charge approves the routing, and without approval nothing goes to the department and nothing becomes public.
work_items.form_name: A suggestion for the appropriate department

work_items.title: The small-numbers rule before publication
work_items.description: The assistant counts how many reports belong to a topic and a neighbourhood, and indicates where there are few.
work_items.prompt: The Data and analysis officer counts how many reports belong to a topic and a neighbourhood, for example how many from Malomsor. Where the number stays below the minimum set by the council (five by default), they do not show the breakdown but merge it with the rest, because the sender could be guessed from it. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only count and draft; the officer in charge approves the publication, and without approval nothing becomes public.
work_items.form_name: The small-numbers rule before publication

work_items.title: We check that every question of the form has a field in the register
work_items.description: The form does not open as long as any of its questions is left without a field.
work_items.prompt: Before opening, the Data and analysis officer goes through the questions of the registration and correction form (for example the name, the address, the parcel number, the phone number and the number of members of the household), and names the register field for each. If even one question has no field, the form does not open, and the gap is reported back by name, so the resident never meets it. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only count the questions without a field and word the gap; whatever is put before the public is approved by a person.
work_items.form_name: We check that every question of the form has a field in the register

work_items.title: We invite the resident to fill it in with a verified contact
work_items.description: Residents enter and correct their own details from their own phone, with their confirmed phone number or email address.
work_items.prompt: At the market, at the gate and at the customer service, the Community liaison shows residents how they can register or correct their own data, for example Szabó Réka from the Malomsor neighbourhood, and sends her the confirmation message to her phone number. Whoever cannot fill it in by phone is helped, and throughout it remains the source of the answer. A person carries out this step, no AI role is in it.
work_items.form_name: We invite the resident to fill it in with a verified contact

work_items.title: The answer goes into the register, and its source is the resident
work_items.description: The answer received creates a new register record or updates the existing one, and the source field shows the resident.
work_items.prompt: The Data and analysis officer puts the answer received into the question's field in the register: if the resident is already in it, the existing record is updated, if not, a new one is created, for example a new household in Kertváros. The source of the record is always the resident themself, with the time. They count how many records were created and how many were updated per neighbourhood. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only record the answer, count the records created and updated, and summarise; whatever is put before the public is approved by a person.
work_items.form_name: The answer goes into the register, and its source is the resident

work_items.title: We keep the contact and the consent together, and show what we store
work_items.description: The resident sees their own record, and their consent is in the same place as their contact details.
work_items.prompt: The Data protection and records officer checks that the resident's contact details and consent are recorded in one place, side by side, and that the resident can at any time see what the register keeps about them. If the resident withdraws consent, their answer stays, but does not appear in the figures and the lists. A person carries out this step, no AI role is in it.
work_items.form_name: We keep the contact and the consent together, and show what we store

work_items.title: A person approves corrections to identifying details
work_items.description: Corrections to the name, address and parcel number are transferred to the existing record only after approval.
work_items.prompt: The Town clerk goes through the corrections that change the name, address or parcel number of an existing record, and approves or rejects them before they are overwritten in the register; the resident receives a confirmation, for example that their correction of 8 November 2026 has taken effect. Until then the old data stays, and the correction shows as a draft. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only summarise how the new data differs from the old and word a reminder for the resident; whatever is put before the public is approved by a person.
work_items.form_name: A person approves corrections to identifying details

work_items.title: We name what we ask consent for, and how long we keep it
work_items.description: The data protection officer describes what the town council asks consent for, how long it keeps it, and what has changed compared with the previous version.
work_items.prompt: The Data protection and records officer lists what the municipality asks consent for (for example for keeping identifiable answers of the Malomsor neighbourhood survey), how long it keeps them (for example 24 months), and what changes compared with the previous version. A person carries out this step, no AI role is in it.
work_items.form_name: We name what we ask consent for, and how long we keep it

work_items.title: We write the new version of the consent text
work_items.description: The town clerk prepares a plain-language text from the summary and shows how it differs from the previous version.
work_items.prompt: Based on the list, the Town clerk words the new version 3 of the consent text, in plain language, and adds a short list of how it differs from version 2. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only prepare a draft and compare the two versions; whatever is put before the public is approved by a person.
work_items.form_name: We write the new version of the consent text

work_items.title: We approve and publish the text
work_items.description: The mayor approves the new version by name, and only then does it take effect.
work_items.prompt: The Mayor / council chair reads version 3, approves it and signs it by name, and only then does it go out as a new, numbered version among the consents; the old versions are kept. Until then we ask nobody for consent with the new text. A person carries out this step, no AI role is in it.
work_items.form_name: We approve and publish the text

work_items.title: We ask for consent, and record which version it was for
work_items.description: The liaison explains what the consent is for, and the register records who accepted which version and when.
work_items.prompt: The Community liaison, at the market, at the gate or on paper, explains what the consent is for, and only after that asks Szabó Mária and the others to say yes. We record in the register who accepted which version and when. Without consent nobody touches the identifiable answers. A person carries out this step, no AI role is in it.
work_items.form_name: We ask for consent, and record which version it was for

work_items.title: We carry out the withdrawal the same day
work_items.description: If someone withdraws their consent, the data protection officer hides their answers and messages on the same day.
work_items.prompt: If someone, for example Horváth Amani, withdraws their consent on any channel, the Data protection and records officer records it the same day, and we hide that person's answers and messages: the report no longer counts them and they do not show in the conversation. We delete nothing: it can be restored, and produced on a legal request. A person carries out this step; no AI role decides on a withdrawal.
work_items.form_name: We carry out the withdrawal the same day

work_items.title: We count what we hid
work_items.description: The analyst counts how many answers and messages we hid, and checks that the report already counts without them.
work_items.prompt: The Data and analysis officer counts how many answers and how many messages the withdrawal hid, by neighbourhood (for example 4 messages and 2 answers in Malomsor), and checks that the report's totals are already stated without them. Gives a number, never a person. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only count and summarise; anything that goes before the public is approved by a person.
work_items.form_name: We count what we hid

work_items.title: We confirm the withdrawal the same day
work_items.description: The communications officer writes to the person who withdrew, saying that it has been done and that it can be restored.
work_items.prompt: The Communications officer writes the confirmation to the person who withdrew the same day: it has been done, what we hid, that we did not delete it, and that it can be restored on request. The outgoing letter is not sent until the Data protection and records officer has approved it. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only prepare a draft and follow up on whether it arrived; anything that goes before the public is approved by a person.
work_items.form_name: We confirm the withdrawal the same day

work_items.title: We choose how to reach each person
work_items.description: The community liaison notes household by household who wants a paper sheet, whom we call by phone, and whom we talk to in person.
work_items.prompt: The Community liaison, talking with people at the Határrét gates and the Malomsor market, notes down who has no smartphone or who is not comfortable with a screen, and agrees with each of them how they would answer: on a paper sheet, in a phone call or in person. Totals up by neighbourhood (Óváros, Kertváros, Malomsor, Határrét) how many households need which way. A person carries out this step; artificial intelligence does not fill it.
work_items.form_name: We choose how to reach each person

work_items.title: We prepare the sheet and the phone script with the same questions
work_items.description: The communications officer drafts the printed sheet, the phone script and the short SMS reminder.
work_items.prompt: We put the round's questions into simple sentences, in the same order, for the printed sheet, the phone script and the short SMS reminder, so that whoever answers on paper, by phone or on the screen gets the same thing. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only draft the sheet, the script and the reminder; anything that goes before the public or into the records is always approved by a person.
work_items.form_name: We prepare the sheet and the phone script with the same questions

work_items.title: We hand out and collect the sheets, and call whoever needs it
work_items.description: The community liaison hands out the sheets, takes answers by phone and in person too, and notes whom they could not reach.
work_items.prompt: The Community liaison hands out the paper sheets at the Malomsor market stall, in the Kertváros associations and at the Határrét gates, phones the people who were asked for following the script (the phone and voice channel are already working), keeps notes on the in-person conversations on the same sheet, and records by neighbourhood whom they could not reach. A person carries out this step; artificial intelligence does not fill it.
work_items.form_name: We hand out and collect the sheets, and call whoever needs it

work_items.title: We send the form for the returned sheets to the district clerk
work_items.description: The system sends the clerk the sheets form; for each sheet they enter on whose behalf the answer must be recorded and how it arrived.
work_items.prompt: The system sends the district clerk the form for the collected paper sheets: the sheets (for example forty from the Malomsor meeting) were brought back by the community liaison. For each sheet the clerk states in whose name the answer is to be recorded, and also whether it came on paper, by phone or in person. A person carries out this step; artificial intelligence does not fill it.
work_items.form_name: Handing over the returned sheets

questions.prompt: On whose behalf should the response be recorded?

work_items.title: We check the consent on every sheet
work_items.description: The data protection and records officer checks that consent is present on every sheet, and hides those with withdrawn consent.
work_items.prompt: The Data protection and records officer goes through the recorded sheets: whether consent shows on each one, and for anyone who withdrew, their answer is hidden, not deleted. Where consent is missing, the sheet is not counted until it is supplied. A person carries out this step; artificial intelligence does not fill it.
work_items.form_name: We check the consent on every sheet

work_items.title: We count once per person, and publish the coverage
work_items.description: The data and analysis officer compares the paper, phone and in-person answers with those given on screen, counts each person once, and says which neighbourhood is missing.
work_items.prompt: We count the answers that came on paper, by phone, in person and on the screen together, once per person, broken down by neighbourhood, and compare them with the number of households to see which neighbourhood was left out. The AI role (RU-AI-1) may only count and compare, and may not publish a name list; anything that goes before the public or into the records is always approved by a person.
work_items.form_name: We count once per person, and publish the coverage

work_items.title: We count how many we invited, by neighbourhood
work_items.description: The denominator comes from the register: how many people we sent the round to.
work_items.prompt: From the register we count, by neighbourhood (Óváros, Kertváros, Malomsor, Határrét), how many people we invited to the round; this is the denominator, and without it coverage cannot be stated. For example, there are 1 240 invitees in Kertváros and 860 in Malomsor. Where the register is thin, we write that down too. The AI role may only count and summarise; in keeping with the rule (RU-AI-1), anything that goes before the public is always approved by a person.
work_items.form_name: We count how many we invited, by neighbourhood

work_items.title: We count the answers once per person
work_items.description: From the same verified contact, only one answer counts in the same round.
work_items.prompt: Compare the answers received with the verified phone numbers and contact details. If a second answer arrives from the same contact in the same round, reject or flag it, and do not count it twice. Write down what we left out and why: duplicate, incomplete answer, answer belonging to another round. For example, of 412 answers received in Malomsor, 391 count and 21 are duplicates. The AI role may only count and summarise; in keeping with the rule (RU-AI-1), anything that goes before the public is always approved by a person.
work_items.form_name: We count the answers once per person

work_items.title: We check that the number makes no one identifiable
work_items.description: A group below the smallest allowed size is merged or left out.
work_items.prompt: The data protection officer goes through the numbers meant for publication: a group below the smallest permitted size, for example three answers from one street, we merge with the neighbouring group or leave out, and we state that we did this. We publish a number, never a person. Only a person may carry out this step; if the round would ask for more than is necessary, the role may stop it.
work_items.form_name: We check that the number makes no one identifiable

work_items.title: We write the coverage notice
work_items.description: The denominator, the respondents, the non-respondents and the skipped answers in one place.
work_items.prompt: Write the coverage statement: the denominator, how many answered by neighbourhood, who did not answer (in numbers, never by name), and what we left out in the earlier steps. Where a neighbourhood's coverage is thin, say so and do not dress it up: the voice of the loudest should not count for the whole neighbourhood. The AI role may only prepare a draft and count; in keeping with the rule (RU-AI-1), anything that goes before the public is always approved by a person.
work_items.form_name: We write the coverage notice

work_items.title: We put our name to the notice
work_items.description: The mayor or the council chair approves before the coverage is published.
work_items.prompt: The mayor or the council chair compares the statement with the numbers and the result of the data protection check, corrects it if needed, and stands behind it with their name. Only a person may carry out this step, because a person is responsible for what goes before the public; without approval, the coverage does not go out.
work_items.form_name: We put our name to the notice

work_items.title: We publish the coverage together with the denominator
work_items.description: On the website and the neighbourhood notice boards, on paper too.
work_items.prompt: After approval, publish the coverage on the town council's website and on the Zöldhalom neighbourhood noticeboards, also on paper beside the gate and the market stall, together with the denominator, and send it to the groups the round reached. A person submits the timing of the announcement and the final form of the text. The AI role may only prepare a draft and remind; in keeping with the rule (RU-AI-1), anything that goes before the public is always approved by a person.
work_items.form_name: We publish the coverage together with the denominator

work_items.title: We assign an amount to the neighbourhood's vote
work_items.description: The Finance officer designates the budget line and determines the amount residents may decide on.
work_items.prompt: The Finance officer designates from the 2026 budget the line that residents may vote on, for example 6 000 000 Ft for the Malomsor neighbourhood, and records how much of it remains for the council's mandatory expenditure. The amount and the line are entered in the accounts so that payment can be made from the same line after the vote. A person carries out this step; no AI role is involved.
work_items.form_name: We assign an amount to the neighbourhood's vote

work_items.title: We gather the residents' proposals
work_items.description: The Consultation lead launches a call and collects by neighbourhood what residents would spend it on.
work_items.prompt: The Consultation lead launches a call to the residents of Óváros, Kertváros, Malomsor and Határrét: what would they spend the neighbourhood's amount on. We receive proposals in such a way that they can also be handed in on paper at the gate and the market stall. The proposals received can be totalled, counted by neighbourhood and drafted onto a uniform sheet. The AI role (RU-AI-1) only drafts, summarises, follows up or counts; anything that goes before the public is approved by a person.
work_items.form_name: We gather the residents' proposals

work_items.title: We review what they cost and whether they are feasible
work_items.description: The Town clerk determines for every proposal the cost and whether the council can do it.
work_items.prompt: For each proposal the Town clerk checks whether it is a task of the town council, what it costs in forints (for example 1 850 000 Ft for renovating the Malomsor playground), and whether it fits within the designated amount. For any proposal not put on the ballot, they write down the reason and tell the person who proposed it. Only what the Town clerk has reviewed can go on the ballot. A person carries out this step; no AI role is involved.
work_items.form_name: We review what they cost and whether they are feasible

work_items.title: We invite residents to vote everywhere
work_items.description: The Communications officer gets the ballot paper to every neighbourhood, on paper too.
work_items.prompt: The Communications officer gets the approved ballot to the residents of every neighbourhood: on the website, on the noticeboards and on paper at the gate and the market stall, and reminds them of the voting deadline. The AI role (RU-AI-1) only drafts the invitation and the reminder, and counts how many people from each neighbourhood have already voted; anything that goes before the public is approved by a person.
work_items.form_name: We invite residents to vote everywhere

work_items.title: We count once per person and rank the proposals
work_items.description: The Data and analysis officer counts the votes and reports turnout by neighbourhood.
work_items.prompt: The Data and analysis officer counts a single vote per person (a second vote from the same person is flagged and not counted), puts the proposals in order by the votes received, and reports by neighbourhood how many of those entitled voted, for example 412 votes in Malomsor. The AI role (RU-AI-1) only counts and summarises; anything that goes before the public is approved by a person.
work_items.form_name: We count once per person and rank the proposals

work_items.title: We decide on the ranking, and publish the winners
work_items.description: The Mayor decides from the ranking what the amount covers, and publishes it.
work_items.prompt: The Mayor, looking over the residents' ranking, decides which proposals the designated amount covers, and publishes the winners and the amount under their own name. If they depart from the residents' ranking, they write the reason in the published report. A person carries out this step; no AI role is involved.
work_items.form_name: We decide on the ranking, and publish the winners

work_items.title: We account for the neighbourhood's spending
work_items.description: The Finance officer enters the winning proposals in the accounts, and reports how much we spent per neighbourhood.
work_items.prompt: The Finance officer enters the winning proposals in the accounts on the neighbourhood's budget line, and reports how much we spent on the items voted for by neighbourhood, and how much of the amount remains. Payment may be authorised only up to the approved limit. A person carries out this step; no AI role is involved.
work_items.form_name: We account for the neighbourhood's spending

work_items.title: We sort the sheets by the way they arrived
work_items.description: The way an answer arrived decides which recording step comes next; what arrived on screen need not be keyed in.
work_items.prompt: The way it arrived decides which recording step comes next: paper, phone or in-person conversation. What arrived on the screen does not have to be typed in by anyone; it goes on to the check. The system carries out this step based on the answer given; artificial intelligence does not fill it.

work_items.title: We record the answers that arrived on paper
work_items.description: The district clerk records the answers that arrived on paper on the round's own form, with the “on whose behalf” field.
work_items.prompt: The district clerk records the answers that arrived on paper (for example forty sheets from the Malomsor meeting) on the round's own form: for every answer they fill in in whose name it is recorded, and mark how it arrived. They use no new screen; the answers go to the same place as those given on the screen. A person carries out this step; artificial intelligence does not fill it.
work_items.form_name: We record the answers that arrived on paper

questions.prompt: On whose behalf did we record the response?

work_items.title: We record the answers that arrived by phone
work_items.description: The district clerk records the answers that arrived by phone on the round's own form, with the “on whose behalf” field.
work_items.prompt: The district clerk records the answers that arrived by phone (the answers of residents called back from their phone number) on the round's own form: for every answer they fill in in whose name it is recorded, and mark how it arrived. They use no new screen; the answers go to the same place as those given on the screen. A person carries out this step; artificial intelligence does not fill it.
work_items.form_name: We record the answers that arrived by phone

questions.prompt: On whose behalf did we record the response?

work_items.title: We record the answers that arrived in person
work_items.description: The district clerk records the answers that arrived in person on the round's own form, with the “on whose behalf” field.
work_items.prompt: The district clerk records the answers that arrived in person (what was said at the market stall and at the gate) on the round's own form: for every answer they fill in in whose name it is recorded, and mark how it arrived. They use no new screen; the answers go to the same place as those given on the screen. A person carries out this step; artificial intelligence does not fill it.
work_items.form_name: We record the answers that arrived in person
